newsitem.title: USA: Fuel pump may be cause of TWA 800 crash-report.
newsitem.headline: Fuel pump may be cause of TWA 800 crash-report.

text.p: A missing fuel pump is the mostly likely cause of the TWA Flight 800 crash that killed all 230 people on board off New York last July, the New York Daily News reported in its Sunday edition.
The tabloid said investigators were trying to find the fuel pump, the size of a 12-ounce (340 gm) soda can, that they believe may be the source of the explosion.

The Boeing 747 exploded in mid-air without warning just 11-1/2 minutes after taking off from New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport on a flight to Paris on July 17, plunging into the Atlantic Ocean off Long Island, New York.
The Daily News quoted Russ Young of Boeing as saying that "everybody" was looking for the elusive pump. "I think everyone will feel better if it is recovered and tested," he said.
Four scallop trawlers continue to dredge the ocean floor for wreckage of Flight 800.
The Daily News said investigators believed that vapours may have leaked from the fuel pump, possibly leading to the explosion.
It said a similar pump may have been at the ignition point of another jet explosion in 1976.

Officials from the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Bureau of Investigation continue to say they are considering three possible causes for the crash -- a bomb, a missile or mechanical failure.
